osuna-ct2-d32.summary: In 1648 Innocent X was renewing his nuncios. Philip IV wanted to keep his own: Giulio Rospigliosi, Archbishop of Tarsus, nuncio at Madrid since 1644 – the future Pope Clement IX. He wrote so to his ambassador to the Pope, Cardinal Gil de Albornoz, in a cipher nobody had read: “there can be no instrument more suitable” for the service of both courts, so the ambassador must not desist “in any case”. The letter survives in two ciphered copies with no decipherment; the key came from another paper in the same family archive, a chapter of a letter by Luis de Haro enciphered for Albornoz in 1649, whose plain-text copy was kept.

osuna-ct11-d1.summary: Key document: the cipher chapter and its plain copy of the time, used to rebuild K2 (lines 1-12) and to test it (lines 13-23); no reading of its own.

osuna-ct2-d16.summary: Key document: cipher original aligned on the plain copy of the time, used to rebuild K1, which does not read the 1648 letter.

osuna-ct2-d20.summary: Key document: transcribed before its plain copy was opened, used to test K1 (0.638 of characters recovered against a 99th percentile of 0.550 for permuted keys).

system: syllabic cipher: syllables “disguised” as other syllables (consonant changed, vowel kept: mo = co, ne = de, ra = sa, la = pa, ti = mi), numbers in series of five (35–39 = la le li lo lu; 45–49 = ra…ru; 50–54 = ta…tu), single letters (2 = n, n = s, m = r, g =…
